name: Mauritanian Thieboudienne
description: Thieboudienne, shared with neighboring Senegal, is Mauritania's national dish - real Mauritanian versions genuinely include cabbage and eggplant alongside the more familiar carrot and okra. Real technique builds the dish in layers: season and fry the fish first, cook the vegetables in the tomato broth, then let the rice absorb everything left in the pot at the end.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

ingredients.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

steps_detailed: Season the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, then fry in a little oil, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden. Set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot, 3-4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and 2 cups water and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the carrot, cabbage, and eggplant, and simmer 12-15 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the okra and simmer 5 minutes more.
Stir in the rice and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender, letting it absorb everything left in the pot.
Return the fried fish to warm through before serving.

name: Mauritanian Mechoui
description: Mechoui, slow-roasted lamb rubbed with real butter, cumin, garlic, and paprika, is Mauritania's traditional centerpiece for special occasions - real technique roasts the meat until it's genuinely tender enough to pull apart by hand, traditionally cooked over embers on a skewered branch.
steps_detailed: Mix the softened butter with the cumin, garlic, and paprika, being generous with the spices, and rub all over the lamb.
Roast at 325F (165C) for 50-60 minutes, basting occasionally, until genuinely fall-apart tender.

name: Mauritanian Mint Tea
description: Mauritanian sweet tea is prepared with a real, distinctive pouring technique called ragwa - raising the teapot high while pouring to build a frothy foam, a genuine ritual repeated across several rounds for guests.
steps_detailed: Warm the tea with the mint 5 minutes.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved.
Pour from a real height into small glasses to build a genuine frothy foam - the ragwa technique, repeated several times, is a real, essential part of Mauritanian hospitality.

name: Mauritanian Mafe (Camel or Beef in Peanut Sauce)
description: Mahfe, meat stewed in a real peanut, okra, and tomato sauce, reflects Mauritania's genuine use of camel meat alongside more common beef - beef stands in here as a widely available substitute.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, add to the pot.
Add the okra and simmer 25-28 minutes until the beef is tender.

description: Mauritanian couscous, real technique steamed two or three times with fluffing between rounds, is prepared numerous ways with vegetable or meat stews.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, carrot, and chickpeas in 1.5 cups water 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Toss the dry couscous with a little oil and water.
Steam over the simmering stew for 10 minutes, then fluff and steam again 8-10 minutes for properly light, separate grains.
Serve the stew and broth over the finished couscous.
